clue.text: Brawl resulting in no charges

definitions.meaning: a brawl is a chaotic fight that everyone joins in
when nobody pays, entry is gratis for everybody

explanation.surface: A street fight ends without anyone being prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' suggests police charges after the brawl, but the second sense is prices: nothing is charged to anybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: a melee with everyone involved, and something given at no cost to anybody.

clue.text: Plump supernatural creature's raised feeling timid

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: an elf is a small supernatural creature; the possessive 's adds no letter
feeling timid means shy

explanation.surface: A chubby fairy creature is feeling bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone plump has plenty of flesh on them, a well-padded build.

clue.text: True-born Englishman turned up carrying dress

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase True-born Englishman is carrying the letters within it, across its words

explanation.surface: A true-born Englishman gets dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'carrying dress' as the definition, but 'carrying' is the hidden-word indicator; the definition is 'dress' alone. EBORNE spans 'trUE BORN Englishman' and turned up gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dress someone is to clothe them in a robe or garments, a formal verb for clothing.

clue.text: Top job that one expects to get next day

definitions.meaning: a first-rate position or appointment, a post of the highest class

definitions.text: that one expects to get next day
definitions.meaning: the British Royal Mail's faster service, aiming to deliver letters the next working day

explanation.surface: A senior role, which one hopes to land by tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain first-class mail is the stamp tier promising next-day delivery, as against slower second-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job, and a first-class one is a top job; it is also the British next-day mail service.

clue.text: Conservative, clever and open to being corrected

parts.note: the political right is the conservative side
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A sharp Tory who is willing to admit mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be put right, a wrong able to be remedied, is open to correction.

clue.text: Wool supplier a series of shops promoted

indicators.note: in a down entry, promoted means moved upward, so the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre, a series of shops

explanation.surface: A wool merchant's chain of stores gets a marketing push.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean animal is kept for its fleece, which is spun into wool.

clue.text: On retirement, cry with son and employer

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the word for cry is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Someone retiring weeps with their son and their old manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the person who employs you and gives the orders at work is your boss.

clue.text: Where chickens may lay eggs at large?

definitions.meaning: a chicken run is the fenced pen where hens live and lay
escaped and not yet caught, as a fugitive is

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful first reading: hens in their run, as against a fugitive evading capture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive at large is evading capture; a hen laying in its pen does so in its fenced run.

clue.text: Irritable cats cry, running wild around hospital

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the hospital letter
running wild says the letters of cats cry are thrown into disorder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Cats yowling as they run riot round a hospital are bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' shuffles CATSCRY into SCRATCY, and 'around' places H within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of tetchy: a scratchy mood is irritable and quick to snap.

clue.text: Go round stirring up a civic argument

indicators.note: stirring up means mixing, so these fourteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Avoiding a council dispute by sidestepping it, or provoking one.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail or travel all the way around something, such as the globe, is to go round it.

clue.text: Dread losing time in blunder

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word for dread

parts.note: terror is extreme dread

explanation.surface: Fear of running out of time leads to a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blunder is a careless mistake, a slip or gaffe.

clue.text: One fights boy going to island captured by dangerous American creature

indicators.note: captured by means the boy and island letters sit inside the creature word

parts.note: gator is American shorthand for an alligator
a lad is a boy
I is the abbreviation for island, as on maps

explanation.surface: A boy heading for an island is caught by an alligator and must fight.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome these were professional combatants who fought in the arena for public entertainment.

clue.text: Normal behaviour at home

parts.note: a habit is one's normal, routine behaviour

explanation.surface: How someone usually behaves when relaxing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' reads as one phrase, but 'at' is wordplay and 'home' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in nature writing: the natural surroundings where an animal or plant lives are its home.

clue.text: Perhaps soldier adopts terribly nice veteran

indicators.note: adopts means the insect word takes the scrambled letters into itself

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, so perhaps flags the example

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of nice are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trooper takes in an awfully pleasant old campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' seems military, but soldiers are a caste of insect in a colony, which 'Perhaps' signals; 'terribly' marks the jumble and 'adopts' the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: an old man, a long-serving veteran, was once called an ancient, and the adjective means very old.

clue.text: Rumble abbot stoned on hard grass?

indicators.note: stoned suggests being out of one's head, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An abbot who is high on cannabis gets found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' and 'stoned' suggest cannabis; here grass is slang for an informer. 'stoned' shuffles RUMBLEABBOT into BLABBERMOUT, with 'on' adding H.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a grass is an informer, someone who cannot keep secrets and tells all, so a tattler.

clue.text: Outgoing leader leaves message: 'Resistance is supported by public'

indicators.note: in a down entry, supported by means the following piece sits underneath
leader leaves means the first letter of the message word goes

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
R is the physics symbol for resistance
overt means open and public

explanation.surface: A departing chief leaves a note saying the resistance has popular backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing leader' looks like a retiring boss, but 'Outgoing' is the definition and 'leader leaves' cuts TEXT to EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outgoing, sociable person is one whose energy is directed outward toward others.

clue.text: Element against capitalism, not English

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: not here says the English letter is left out

parts.note: capitalism is the system built on money and capital

explanation.surface: An anti-capitalist who refuses to be English.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: this is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb, atomic number 51.

clue.text: Being filmed ruined a romance

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of a romance are rearranged

explanation.surface: A love affair is spoiled by its being caught on film.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone in front of a recording camera, appearing in the shot, is being filmed.

clue.text: Suspect online assent is unimportant

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Agreeing to terms online with a click is dubious and doesn't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something not essential is not needed, so of little importance.

clue.text: Ring about manuscript being twisted and miserable

indicators.note: about means the phone word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to ring a number is to dial it

indicators.note: being twisted means the manuscript abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A phone call about a mangled manuscript leaves someone gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dismal means gloomy and depressing, causing or showing misery.

clue.text: Gambler improved

definitions.meaning: one who bets, a punter placing wagers
made or become superior to before

explanation.walkthrough: The noun splits as bet + -ter, one who bets; the other sense is the comparative of good.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who bets; the other is the verb meaning made superior, as in bettered.

clue.text: Changing to spin restricts amateur's start on a sticky wicket

indicators.note: restricts means the scrambled letters hem in another piece
changing means the letters of to spin are altered in order
the start of the word means its first letter

explanation.surface: A bowler switching to spin when an amateur batsman starts on a difficult pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sticky wicket is a cricket pitch made treacherous by rain, hence a tough situation. 'Changing' turns TOSPIN into INSPOT, and 'restricts' encloses A.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in a tricky predicament is being on a sticky wicket, a difficult situation.

clue.text: Run rising European business

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly

explanation.surface: European business is on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: trade is commerce, the business of buying and selling goods.

clue.text: Opening offer disheartened journalist having to leave building

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of offer stay
having to leave means the journalist's letters are removed from the building word

parts.note: an edifice is a large building
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A dispirited reporter forced out of an office building receives an opening offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening offer' reads as one phrase, but 'Opening' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an orifice is a hole or vent in the body or an object, an opening.

clue.text: Exaggerate love with rubbish in poem

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: in means the rubbish word goes inside the poem word

parts.note: verse means poetry, a poem
tat is shoddy rubbish

explanation.surface: Overdoing love by stuffing junk into a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exaggerate is to claim more than the truth, stating a case too strongly.

clue.text: Acknowledge passage with marks to be taken in

indicators.note: to be taken in means the marks letter is placed inside the passage word

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine
M stands for marks, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Conceding a corridor where scuffs must be absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a mining tunnel; marks were Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to acknowledge a fact or fault is to concede or confess it.

clue.text: Amount of money earned in a certain period

indicators.note: an amount of the phrase means only a portion of its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: How much one earns over a fixed span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests annual income; the letters run across 'moneY EARned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: twelve months is a fixed span of time, a certain period.

clue.text: Outsmart rep number one

parts.note: to best someone is to outsmart them
a sales rep is a seller

explanation.surface: A salesman who outwits everyone becomes top of the sales chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A number one on the chart is a book or record that sells more copies than any rival.
